I am a 47-year-old woman farming in Machinga with no schooling, but I know this land well. This 0.20 hectare plot is where I grow my maize, intercropped with some beans and pigeon pea, and it must feed my family. I was lucky to receive a FISP coupon this season, so I will apply some NPK and urea here—though I have to stretch it across all my plots—and I will plant the hybrid seed they gave me because it yields better. I also have a small pile of composted manure to mix in. We do not spray chemicals or use irrigation here; the rains are our only water. My children and I will do all the planting, weeding, and harvesting with our hoes, and I will not hire ganyu labor because money is too tight for that.
